clue.text: Queen, perhaps, with European renown but no line in class

indicators.note: 'but no' tells us to drop the thing named, and a line is the letter abbreviated L

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so a cat is a queen's general kind
E is the abbreviation for European
glory is fame or renown

explanation.surface: A queen's fame comes without any line of descent, hinting at royalty in a class system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks royal but is a female cat. GLORY loses its L to leave GORY, giving CAT + E + GORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a class or division of things sharing some characteristic.

clue.text: US writer, one first off to receive a prize

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the next pieces go inside
the first letter is taken off the front of the word

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
taken as written
a pot is a trophy or prize, or the stake won

explanation.surface: An American author is the first person to drop out of contention before receiving an award.
explanation.walkthrough: ACE loses its A to leave CE, which then holds A POT. Truman Capote wrote Breakfast at Tiffany's.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was an American novelist, author of In Cold Blood.

clue.text: Put limit on number south of Thailand

indicators.note: in a down clue, being south means coming lower, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: T is Thailand's international vehicle registration code
a number is something that numbs, and ether was used as an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A numerical cap is placed somewhere south of Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a figure, but here is a thing that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To tether an animal is to tie it, restricting how far it can roam, so it limits movement.

clue.text: It could be angered about a trespasser's entry?

definitions.text: It could be angered about a trespasser's entry?

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the rest
'could be' suggests a possible version of the word, so its letters can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the entry point of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of trespasser

explanation.surface: A guard dog might be riled at an intruder coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a big guard dog might well be riled by an intruder. ANGERED is rearranged round A and the T of trespasser.
explanation.definitionFit: A Great Dane is a huge breed of dog, the kind that might growl angrily at an intruder.

clue.text: Trumpeter's last note after playing musical composition

indicators.note: 'after' places one piece behind the other in order
the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of trumpeter
an actor or player is on when performing
do is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A trumpeter's final note at the end of a performance of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme returns between contrasting sections.

clue.text: Tawdry gear put in front of school

indicators.note: placing one item ahead of the other fixes their order, first thing then second

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear
SCH is the standard abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: Cheap, showy equipment is placed at the front of a school building.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch describes art or objects in poor, showy taste, which is what tawdry means as an adjective.

clue.text: Cool stop for non-mainstream band

parts.note: something in is fashionable or cool
to die is to stop, as an engine does

explanation.surface: A trendy place to stop for an alternative group.
explanation.definitionFit: An indie band is one on an independent label, outside the commercial mainstream.

clue.text: Model under the influence of drink? Don't move!

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: An artist's model who has been drinking is told to stay still.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit tight is the idiom for staying put and taking no action, as the exclamation commands.

clue.text: Many see around back of older pub

parts.note: a host is a great number or multitude

indicators.note: 'around' means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is the crossword's favourite one

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of older

explanation.surface: Crowds look around the back of an ageing pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' here is a diocese: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire. HOST + EL(R)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an old-fashioned or humorous word for an inn or pub.

clue.text: Posh baronet in cultivated style shows refinement

indicators.note: 'in' places the earlier pieces inside the other
cultivated ground is worked over, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
U means upper class, from the old U and non-U distinction
BT is the abbreviation for baronet

explanation.surface: An upper-class baronet with a polished manner displays elegance.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a British convention. U + BT goes inside a rearranged STYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtlety is delicacy and finesse of perception or manner, which is what refinement denotes.

clue.text: Sample sales talk close to salesman

parts.note: patter is a salesperson's glib, rehearsed talk

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of salesman

explanation.surface: A salesman offers a sample alongside his pitch, nearing the end of the sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern can be a specimen or model used as an example, such as a fabric swatch shown to customers.

clue.text: Past due to be reviewed in bulletins, say

indicators.note: something reviewed is looked over again and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Overdue items are to be looked at again in news bulletins.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulletins are one example of news reports bringing people the latest information, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Discuss free entertainment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to deal with a subject in speech or writing
second meaning: something paid for by another person as a kindness

explanation.surface: Someone proposes talking about a complimentary show.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a topic is to discuss it, and a treat is a pleasure someone else pays for on your behalf.

clue.text: How one might describe caller at risk?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone phoning is connected by telephone
second meaning: in jeopardy, exposed to danger

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: a telephone caller is literally connected by wire, while the idiom means one's job or reputation is in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being in jeopardy also literally describes someone currently speaking on the telephone.

clue.text: Actress ferries chair in play

indicators.note: something in play is moving about freely, so these letters are loose to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stage actress carries a chair around during a theatrical production.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrie Fisher was the American performer famous for playing Princess Leia in the Star Wars films.

clue.text: Minister never flustered when indebted?

indicators.note: 'when indebted' means placed in a state of debt, so the jumbled letters sit inside the colour of debt

parts.note: being in debt is being in the red

indicators.note: someone flustered is agitated and confused, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman stays calm even when he owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: Being in the red means being overdrawn at the bank, so 'indebted' here places the jumbled letters inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverend is a member of the clergy, a minister of religion.

clue.text: Novel learning covering English mostly

indicators.note: covering something means going over and around it, so one piece encloses the other
novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Fresh knowledge mainly involves studying the English language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' looks like an instruction to cut a word, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean usually or on the whole, describing what holds true in most cases.

clue.text: Wonderful part of a tennis player's repertoire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for excellent

definitions.text: part of a tennis player's repertoire
definitions.meaning: second meaning: hitting the ball down hard from overhead

explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal British praise for something excellent, and also the act of hitting overhead tennis shots downward hard.

clue.text: Dismiss idiot overlooking latest in computer protection

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the final letter is left out

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job
wally is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A manager sacks a fool who ignored the latest computer security update.
explanation.definitionFit: A firewall is software or hardware that blocks unauthorised network traffic from reaching a computer.

clue.text: Frenchman to support diplomat and get on initial trip?

parts.note: M is the abbreviation of Monsieur
to aid is to help or support
an envoy is a diplomatic representative
to get on in years is to grow older

explanation.surface: A Frenchman backs an ambassador and boards a ship on a first journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' suggests boarding, but here means growing older. M + AID + ENVOY + AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden voyage is the first journey made by a new ship, so it is literally an initial trip.

clue.text: One known for snapping American plant

parts.note: a croc, short for crocodile, snaps its jaws
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A photographer from the United States, known for taking snaps, plants something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapping' suggests photography, but it is the jaws of a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocus is a small spring-flowering plant grown from a corm.

clue.text: Act foolishly and get lost

definitions.meaning: first meaning, respaced: ..., tit being British slang for an idiot
second meaning: go away, clear off

explanation.walkthrough: Read the letters as BE A TIT for the first sense; tit is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a curt command to go away, which is what telling someone to get lost means.

clue.text: Noted West Indian that's smuggled in fish? Suspect something wrong

indicators.note: contraband smuggled in is hidden inside something else, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a smelt is a small silvery fish
Brian Lara is a famous West Indies cricketer

explanation.surface: A famous Caribbean figure is caught smuggling something inside a fish, rousing suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means famous, not written down; the setter means the cricketer Brian Lara.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is the idiom for sensing that something is amiss or that deception is going on.

clue.text: See anger in foreign banker

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone notices the fury of an overseas financier.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker in crosswords is often a river, since it has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is a river in France, so a foreign one, and rivers have banks.

clue.text: Follow recorded music

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to trail or pursue
second meaning: one song on an album

explanation.definitionFit: To track something is to trace its path, and a track is a single piece of music on a record.

clue.text: Taverner verifying bottles or bottle?

indicators.note: a bottle holds its contents inside, so these words contain the wanted run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A pub landlord checking whether he stocks bottles or just one bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, which is the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve and bottle both mean courage or daring, bottle being informal British usage.

clue.text: Waiter in trat, possibly, over to secure a gratuity (not pennies)

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the assembled string is read from the far end
'not' removes something, and pennies are abbreviated by a single letter that must go

parts.note: to nail is to fasten or secure
taken as written
a tip is a gratuity

explanation.surface: A trattoria waiter, perhaps, turns over a tip after pocketing a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: A trat is short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant. TIP loses its P to TI; NAIL + A + TI is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiter working in a trattoria would very likely be a native of Italy, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: A cup includes a lot of sumptuous fruit

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
a pot is a trophy cup

indicators.note: most but not all of a word is wanted, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: rich food or furnishings are sumptuous

explanation.surface: A cup holds a large helping of luxurious fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit, related to the peach and plum.

clue.text: Place to prepare food in area of theatre not right

indicators.note: 'not' removes, and right is abbreviated by a single letter that must be dropped

parts.note: the gallery is the highest seating area in a theatre

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a kitchen in an unsuitable part of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is the kitchen on a ship or aircraft where meals are cooked.

clue.text: Head of school to take out group showing range of talent?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of school
to take someone out is slang for to kill them
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A headteacher removes a class that displays a variety of abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out' looks like a school trip, but means kill.
explanation.definitionFit: A skill set is the full range of abilities and expertise a person possesses.
